sources.entry: Happy Coder by GrocerPublishAgent - Spawn and control multiple Claude Codes in parallel from your phone or desktop. Happy Coder runs Claude Code on your hardware, sends push notifications when Claude needs more input or permission, and costs nothing. End-to-end encrypted, with realtime voice.

summary.one_liner: Happy is an open-source (MIT) mobile, web, and CLI app for running Claude Code, Codex and other AI coding agents on your own hardware and controlling them from your phone, with end-to-end encryption.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the Happy mobile app (iOS, Android, web, built with Expo), the original `happy` CLI that wraps Claude Code and Codex in a terminal, and the relay server used for encrypted sync between devices. Running `happy claude` or `happy codex` starts the agent locally, and the same session can be continued from a phone. The README describes a wider multi-model "Happy Harness" for the separate desktop app, which supports Claude, Codex, Grok, Gemini (via Antigravity), and OpenCode or Agent Client Protocol agents. It says users can sign in with their existing Claude, Codex, and Grok subscriptions. Sessions can be shared with another person, who can watch and steer the same agent. Projects remain ordinary local folders. The README lists sibling repositories for the desktop app, the agent runtime, and the website.
use_cases: Control Claude Code from a phone while away from the desk
Continue a terminal coding session on a mobile device
Run Codex or Claude Code sessions on your own machine remotely
Share a live AI coding session with a colleague
Orchestrate multiple AI coding agents in one interface
Use existing AI subscriptions with a self-hosted agent harness
notable: End-to-end encrypted sync between phone, web, and terminal sessions
Multi-model harness covering Claude, Codex, Grok, Gemini, and OpenCode in the desktop app
Multiplayer sessions where collaborators can watch and steer the same agent
Reuses existing Claude, Codex, and Grok subscription logins instead of separate API billing
caveats: The README steers multi-model and team use toward the separate desktop app and Happy Harness, not this repository's CLI
Mobile, web, CLI and relay server are split across several repositories, so a full setup involves multiple components
Gemini access goes through Antigravity, which the README does not further describe
keywords: run ai coding on my own machine
